objects.original: Euclidean vectors of completed scalar Ito rows.
objects.reconstructed: Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(mu x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Define X(t,omega)=(A_i(t,omega)+sum_j I_T^j(eta_ij)(t,omega))_{i in I}. The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).
objects.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoEuclideanRowRegularity.lean:13; X is constructed with WithLp.toLp from the actual scalar row representatives.

domains.original: Finite state and Brownian coordinate types, finite measure, usual filtration, T>0.
domains.reconstructed: Omega measurable; I,J finite, with decidable equality required for J only; mu finite; filtration on R_+; T>0; B:R_+ x Omega->R^J; eta:I x J->ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,mu,T); A:I x R_+ x Omega->R; X takes values in Euclidean R^I.
domains.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoEuclideanRowRegularity.lean:13; Only J needs DecidableEq; finite I suffices for the product measurable/topological structure.

quantifiers.original: Each drift slice up to T is a.e. measurable; each drift coordinate is a.e. path-continuous; conclude every slice measurable and one a.e. vector-path event.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universally spaces and instances,filtration,mu,T,B; Brownian,positive-T,usual hypotheses; eta,A; then for every i and t<=T the measurability hypothesis, and for every i an a.e. continuity hypothesis. Conclusion: every t<=T has measurable X_t, and almost every omega has a continuous X-path on [0,T].
quantifiers.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoEuclideanRowRegularity.lean:13; The conjunction has ordinary forall time measurability and a.e. path continuity in the correct order.

assumptions.original: Progressive L² noise rows and a.e. continuous drift paths; no BV or adaptedness of drifts.
assumptions.reconstructed: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are mu-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every mu-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). For all i and t<=T, A_i(t,.) is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. For each i, mu-a.e. omega, A_i(.,omega) is continuous on [0,T]. Bounded variation and adaptedness of A are not required.
assumptions.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoEuclideanRowRegularity.lean:13; No BV or drift-progressivity binder is present.

conclusion.original: Measurable X_t for every t≤T and a.e. continuous vector paths on [0,T].
conclusion.reconstructed: every t<=T has measurable X_t, and almost every omega has a continuous X-path on [0,T].
conclusion.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoEuclideanRowRegularity.lean:13; The local mu.IsComplete instance is derived from hUsual.completeAt and filtration.le; nullMeasurable.measurable_of_complete justifies the stronger measurable claim.

scopes.original: Actual measurable slices, not merely completed representatives.
scopes.reconstructed: Slice measurability is pointwise in time. The finite collection of a.e. coordinate continuity assumptions yields the asserted one a.e. event for the vector path. All claims are restricted to [0,T].
scopes.evidence: AutoSamplingTheory/TechnicalLemmas/StochasticProcesses/ItoEuclideanRowRegularity.lean:13; Finite intersection of hA and pointwise continuity of the completed integrals gives one event on [0,T].
